overview: White plays 2.h4 against the fianchetto, planning h5 to open the h-file against ...g6. Black can meet it calmly with ...Bg7 and ...d6 or ...h5 to stop the pawn. No material is given and White keeps a flexible set-up.

white_ideas.idea: Push h5 to break the g6 pawn and open the h-file
Develop Nf3, e4 and Be3 while Black spends tempi

black_ideas.idea: Stop the h-pawn with ...h5 and then play ...Bg7
Counter in the centre with ...d5 or ...c5

typical_structures.structure: Flank pawn storm against a fianchetto
Flexible centre with e4 or d4 still open

character.notes: A wing pawn lunge at move two, with both kings likely to face concrete threats.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; 2.h4 is a pawn advance only.

soundness.notes: The h-pawn push is committal and most strong players think Black is fine.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided at this early stage.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly choose 1.Nc3 and 2.h4 against ...g6.

level.notes: Not a repertoire line players learn first.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...h5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black blocks the h-pawn and White has to find a plan with Bg5 or e4.

character.reason: A wing pawn advance on move two commits both kings to risk.

soundness.reason: The h4 push is considered over-ambitious but not clearly bad.

structure.reason: The centre has not been decided yet.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever choose 1.Nc3 and 2.h4 against ...g6.

level.reason: A dubious flank pawn push is not Beginner and has no heavy theory.

plans.reason: The h-pawn is the whole idea of the line.
